messages:
Sam (Support): getting flood of 401s from multiple customers around 09:48 UTC, tickets piling up. Example: dedicated-tenant-12, API calls returning "invalid_token". noticed a spike in auth-related errors in the dashboard. any visibility? :eyes:
Anya (SRE): saw alerts from token-introspect latency + error rate at 09:46. opening a Sev2 for now. taking a look at logs.
Sam (Support): one customer noted "Authorization failed after maintenance window" — they said they had an active session. Haven't changed client integration.
Kevin (Runtime): tagging @Anya - recent key rotation job ran at 03:00 UTC earlier today (minor rollout). Could that be related? We rotated a signing key and kept an overlap window, but introspection uses JWKS cache.
Anya (SRE): good call. looking at token-introspector pods, cache misses spiked. logs show signature verification failures:
```
ERROR token-introspect: signature verification failed: kid not found in jwks map
trace: /srv/introspect/verify.go:87
```
Anya (SRE): the kid mismatch implies some pods still expect the old jwk mapping or the JWKS endpoint served a different set during rotation.
Oliver (Infra): JWKS service (auth-jwks) had a short rollout at 03:01 — I can see the service returned a mixed set for ~20s because the rollout order updated replicas one at a time without warming. Might be a cache invalidation edge.
Sam (Support): customers getting 401 on both hosted API and dedicated endpoints? Claire, any billing impact flagged?
Claire (Billing): we've seen a handful of usage drops for affected tenants, customers are asking for credits. waiting on SRE confirmation of root cause before recommending adjustments.
Anya (SRE): reproducing locally: if introspector receives a token with kid X but the local jwks cache has only Y, it fails. However, earlier we had a fallback path that queried remote jwks but that path got rate-limited due to sudden burst and returned 429s. logs: 
```
WARN jwks-fetch: 429 Too Many Requests when refreshing jwks for issuer https://auth.redwood.test/.well-known/jwks.json
```
Kevin (Runtime): why did the fallback go to network? we should have used a rolling update strategy that keeps both keys available for the full overlap. Looks like the rotation job removed 'old' key slightly earlier than expected. check rotation script:
```bash
# excerpts from rotation script
PUT /jwks -> replace file, then signal pods
# missing: wait for configmap propagation & cache TTL expiration
```
Oliver (Infra): confirmed - the job replaced the JWKS resource instead of adding the new key alongside the old one. Combined with a 30s cache TTL and pod restart order, some pods had stale copies and started rejecting tokens.
Anya (SRE): mitigation plan: 1) extend jwks cache TTL to 5m to avoid flaps 2) re-add old key to jwks endpoint so both kids valid 3) restart token-introspect pods to pick consistent jwks state. rolling patch now.
sre-bot: Incident SEV2 declared | runbook: auth-introspect-401s | pageresponse: assigned to oncall
deploy-bot: triggered rollout restart for deployment/token-introspector in namespace redwood-auth (3 pods)
Anya (SRE): executing command to restart pods: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/token-introspector -n redwood-auth` — watching for 200/healthy and reduced error rates.
Anya (SRE): after restart, error rate dropped ~90% within 40s. dashboards show 200 responses returning.
Kevin (Runtime): pushed an emergency patch to rotation job to change behavior: now it writes additive JWKS (new key appended) and waits for 10m overlap, then removes older key after confirmation. Patch diff posted in the patch PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge/PR-4321
Sam (Support): customers reporting recovery, some still seeing intermittent 401s — telling them we're patching the rotation job and will follow up with timeline. using canned message: "We're investigating auth errors; mitigation in progress; will follow up once stable."
Claire (Billing): customers asking for RCA and credit; I'll hold until postmortem. please include customer impact window and remediation steps.
Anya (SRE): next steps: 1) full postmortem (root cause: destructive JWKS replacement during rotation + insufficient overlap + JWKS fetch rate limits), 2) action items: change rotation script, increase jwks cache TTL, add rate-limit backoff, add canary key propagation check before removal, 3) contact affected tenants with timeline.
Kevin (Runtime): also adding integration test in CI that exercises JWKS rotation against a local cluster to catch this.
Oliver (Infra): creating infra ticket INFRA-987 to revert rollout order rules and ensure configmaps and JWKS updates are atomic.
Sam (Support): filing a consolidated customer note and will coordinate with Solutions for affected tenants.
Anya (SRE): marking incident as resolved at 10:04 UTC pending postmortem; will run follow-up postmortem sync 11:30.
Sam (Support): thanks — leaving this thread open for postmortem draft + customer list. :thumbsup:
